text: Yazidism is the faith of the Yazidis, a Kurdish-speaking people whose homeland is Kurdistan.
More than 850 years ago, a holy man, Sheikh Adi, settled in the valley of Lalish and united the Yazidi tribes.
src: Yazidism is the ethnic religion of the Kurdish-speaking Yazidis / Kurdistan, from a pre-Islamic Kurdish religious substratum
the central saint of the faith / Sheikh Adi ibn Musafir settles in the valley of Lalish, unites the scattered Yazidi tribes

text: Yazidis believe in one God, who gave the world to seven angels led by Tawûsî Melek, the Peacock Angel.
Their sacred hymns, the qewls, are handed down by word of mouth and sung by their religious leaders.
src: Yazidis believe in one God who created the world and entrusted it to seven angels, led by Tawûsî Melek, the Peacock Angel
The qewls, the sacred hymns, are the most authoritative form / handed down orally / The clergy sing them to set melodies at rites and festivals

text: Yazidis remember 74 farmans, attacks meant to destroy them, over many centuries.
In 2014 the Islamic State attacked Sinjar, killed more than 5,000 Yazidis and carried off thousands of women and girls.
src: Yazidis remember 74 farmans, campaigns of destruction

text: Today most Yazidis of the Middle East live in Iraq, and more than 230,000 live in Germany.
New Yazidi temples opened near Tbilisi in 2015 and in Armenia in 2019.
